system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Overall assessment:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" from our side of the table. It departs from the playbook on almost every liability-regime point, collapses the Fundamental/Title regime into the general cap, and leaves the two pre-Completion deliverables that matter most (Bluefen consent and Riverlark payout) unresolved. Notably, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter is quite candid about the gaps — we should use its admissions against the Seller Update's positions.

A general note on the Seller's drafting device: the Update repeatedly says a limitation "applies to all Claims" / "all Claims of any nature" (cl. 12.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5, and "Tax/IP settled under the general regime"). Read together, these clauses are an attempt to drive every category — Title, Tax, IP, fraud, specific indemnities, payment/covenant claims — through the 20% / 18-month / AUD 250,000 funnel. That cross-cutting override is the single most important thing to reject, because fixing the cap number alone would leave the override intact.

---

## 1. Liability regime — departures from playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority (none given) | **Reject.** Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% figure is not available to us at this stage — do not signal flexibility. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** 5x our position. Counter at AUD 5,000. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, **excess-only** | AUD 50,000, **first dollar** | **Reject on both number and mechanism.** The excess-only ("deductible") structure is a second, hidden cap. Counter at AUD 50,000 tipping basket. |
| Time limit (12.3) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given) | **Reject.** Counter at 24 months. |
| "All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated" (12.3/13) | Blanket override | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | **Reject outright.** This is the structural problem described above. |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | **Reject.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title to the shares we are paying AUD 24m for at AUD 4.8m. Must be a standalone regime. |
| Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct | Not carved out anywhere; 9.3/12.8/20.5 purport to apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature" | Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; non-waivable | **Reject.** A limitation or non-reliance clause that purports to cover fraud is likely unenforceable in any event, but we should not rely on that — insert an express, non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out across cl. 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5. |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution | **Reject the characterisation.** Nothing has been agreed. Tax and IP warranties/indemnities need their own cap and period (to be negotiated); we should not accept "settled" language or a silent fold into the 20%/18-month regime. |

**Reasoning on structure:** the right architecture is tiered — (a) general warranties at 25%/24 months with AUD 5k/AUD 50k thresholds; (b) Fundamental/Title at 100%/6+ years, no thresholds; (c) Tax and IP on separate terms (open); (d) specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006 if needed, bonuses) outside the warranty caps and baskets; (e) fraud etc. outside everything. The Seller's draft has one tier.

---

## 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]:** The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records. This is whole-data-room plus public-register deemed disclosure — exactly what the playbook rejects. The Letter's own clause [11] ("The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts… against the complete agreement and current due diligence record") is effectively a general sweep designed to shift the diligence burden to us.

**Push back:** require that only matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter qualify the warranties. Delete the data-room-as-a-whole and public-register limbs. Numbered specific disclosures (§2–§10) can stand as specific disclosures, but note that most of them disclose a *gap* rather than a fact (e.g. "no final consent included") — a disclosure that something is missing should not operate to qualify a warranty that it exists.

**Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge):** blanket exclusion for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, *including anything discoverable* from the data room or public records. The "discoverable" limb is a constructive-knowledge bar — it means we lose claims for matters we never actually found. Combined with [1.1], this makes the warranties close to illusory.

**Push back:** delete 8.3. If the Seller insists on a knowledge qualifier anywhere, it must be (i) actual knowledge, (ii) of named Buyer individuals only (not "advisers"), (iii) of the specific matter and that it would give rise to a Claim, and (iv) never applying to Title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity. Any seller "knowledge" qualifiers in the warranties themselves must name seller knowledge persons and include a reasonable-enquiry standard.

---

## 3. Conditions and Completion deliverables

### Bluefen (cl. 3 / 6.3) — material
- ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30% of the business. Change-control clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3.
- Seller offers *reasonable endeavours* and deems the condition satisfied *on delivery* of the counterparty's written consent.
- The Disclosure Letter (§2) confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.

**Push back:** the condition must be (a) receipt of an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent in a form reasonably acceptable to the Buyer, and (b) evidence that each 11.3 condition has been satisfied, both before Completion. "Satisfied on delivery" would let a consent with unmet conditions trigger Completion. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a 30%-of-revenue customer; require all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours plus a Buyer-approved form of consent and a step-plan. Also add a Bluefen-specific warranty and consider a pre-Completion undertaking not to vary the Bluefen contract.

### Riverlark (cl. 2 / 7) — material
- ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
- Seller proposes release "following Completion." Disclosure Letter §3 confirms not repaid, no discharge included.

**Push back:** this is a debt-free/cash-free deal. Require: (i) a current payout letter from Riverlark as a Completion deliverable; (ii) repayment directly from Completion funds via the funds flow; (iii) executed security releases (PPSR discharges, release deeds, any share mortgage/guarantee releases) delivered at Completion, or at minimum in escrow against payout. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark (not the Seller) and Amelia Frost's approval — neither exists. Also check whether the 8.1 change-of-control provision has been or needs to be waived to avoid a default between signing and payout.

---

## 4. Price-affecting items

### Employee bonuses (DD-005) — AUD 420,000 plus on-costs
Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised; Disclosure Letter §5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and silent on payroll tax/superannuation/on-costs. These are Company liabilities triggered by Completion — if the Company pays them post-Completion we bear them.

**Push back:** either a specific line item in the funds flow (deduction from price / paid from Seller proceeds through the Company at Completion) or a Seller-funded mechanism, grossed up for payroll tax, super and any other on-costs. Obtain a schedule of recipients, amounts and conditions. Consider a specific indemnity as a backstop.

### Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1 / DD-004 / DD-010)
Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The Seller's indemnity is confined to the SOW3 payment.

**Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to or right to use the Ironquay-developed materials (including third-party claims, re-procurement and cure costs), not just the AUD 180k fee. Preserve the SOW3 cure path: require the Seller to procure cleared payment and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay before Completion, or escrow for it. Note the AUD 180,000 is unverified either way — do not accept it as the ceiling, and do not assert it as a confirmed liability.

### Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) — AUD 330,000
Seller labels them ordinary-course. Disclosure Letter §8 admits it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Assessment:** per playbook, no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Request the contracts and timing; assess whether any amount is accrued/prepaid or committed pre-Completion for post-Completion benefit, and treat through the working-capital / Debt definitions accordingly. Keep this as an open DD item, not a price point yet.

---

## 5. Export / privacy incident (DD-006)
~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address. Investigation preliminary; no confirmed access, scope or notification conclusion; no loss figure. Seller characterises it as "not expected to be material."

**Assessment:** consistent with playbook, we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. But "not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion, not a fact, and must not be accepted as a disclosure that qualifies the data-protection warranties.

**Push back:** (i) pre-Completion undertaking to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation and provide updates to the Buyer; (ii) a Completion-date bring-down of the incident status; (iii) privacy/data warranties unqualified by DD-006 except to the extent of the specific facts stated; (iv) consider a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, sized once the investigation concludes.

---

## 6. Title
Seller: title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012." Disclosure Letter §10 acknowledges this is simply the source relied on, not independent verification.

**Push back:** the register is a Seller-supplied internal document. Require independent evidence: ASIC company extract and share-structure history, constitution, board minutes/share certificates, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, confirmation of no encumbrances over the shares (including under the Riverlark security), and Seller capacity/authority evidence (board/shareholder approvals). Title and capacity warranties must sit in the Fundamental regime (§1 above).

---

## 7. Lesser items
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification only, not landlord consent. Confirm by reading the lease; require the notification to be given as a Completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** restriction on assignment, apparently not triggered by a share sale. Confirm there is no change-of-control limb; warrant accordingly.
- **Disclosure Letter [1.4] (non-admission):** acceptable in principle, but it cannot be used to turn specific disclosures into non-disclosures; ensure it is subordinate to the fair-disclosure standard.

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright**
1. The "all limitations apply to all Claims" override (12.3/13) and the "all Claims of any nature" scope of 9.3/12.8/20.5 — restore separate regimes.
2. Folding Fundamental/Title into the general cap — standalone 100% cap, ≥6 years, no thresholds, no knowledge bar.
3. Absence of a fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out — insert, non-waivable, across all limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses.
4. Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure — replace with specific fair disclosure.
5. Clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion (especially "discoverable") — delete; never applies to Title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
6. "Tax/IP settled" — not agreed; remain open on separate terms.

**Counter**
7. Cap: 25% / AUD 6.0m (no authority for 20%).
8. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 tipping, not deductible.
9. Claims period 24 months (no authority for 18).

**Completion mechanics**
10. Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence of 11.3 conditions satisfied, pre-Completion, Buyer-approved form; endeavours standard raised.
11. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion; post-Completion release only with irrevocable Riverlark undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
12. DD-005 bonuses: specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, grossed up for on-costs.
13. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR/constitutional evidence, not DD-012 alone.

**Specific indemnities / covenants**
14. Ironquay: broaden indemnity; procure payment and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion (cure preserved); AUD 180k treated as unverified.
15. DD-006: preserve logs, investigate, update, bring-down; indemnity sized after investigation; no acceptance of "not material."
16. Sandbar: assess against working-capital/Debt definitions; no automatic deduction.

**Escalations needed:** none of the Seller's fallback-level numbers (20% cap, 18 months) can be accepted without written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft; none exists. Recommend the mark-up go out at full playbook positions.
=== END ADVICE ===
